title: The Right Hand of God: A Psychotherapist's Case for the Reality of the Living God
author: Dale M. Sides, Th.D.
target_audience: Christians seeking to deepen or question their faith
Individuals interested in the intersection of psychology and spirituality
Psychologists, counselors, or therapists exploring spiritual dimensions
Readers interested in personal testimony of spiritual encounters
Those struggling with doubt or seeking experiential evidence of God
core_themes: The living reality of God in the modern world
Personal transformation through encounter with the divine
Case studies as evidence for spiritual realities
The power of faith in psychological healing
primary_purpose: To present a compelling argument, based on clinical experience and real-life cases, that God is active, real, and personally accessible in the world today, offering psychological healing and transformation.

structure_format.narrative_style: Personal, testimonial, and analytical; combines case studies with theological reflection
structure_format.organization: Chapters structured around key concepts, personal experiences, and case histories

key_concepts_lessons: God's presence is both experiential and evidential in the lives of individuals.
Psychotherapy can validate and even facilitate genuine spiritual experiences.
Faith has transformative power for psychological and emotional healing.
Integrative practice between psychology and faith can yield profound therapeutic results.
Skepticism toward spiritual claims can be addressed through careful documentation of real-world phenomena.
notable_features: Bridges clinical psychology with Christian faith
Presents real-world case studies as evidence
Draws from author's personal and clinical journeys
Offers both practical therapeutic perspectives and faith-based insights
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 21st century during an era of growing interest in the compatibility of science (in this case, psychology) and faith, and at a time when practitioners and patients alike explored more holistic approaches to mental health.
reception_impact: Valued in Christian counseling and spiritual formation circles
Appreciated by those seeking personal accounts of God's reality
Contributed to dialogues between psychology and religion
May be met with skepticism by academically secular therapists or readers requiring empirical evidence
comparable_titles: Care of Souls: Revisioning Christian Nurture and Counsel by David G. Benner
Healing the Soul of a Woman by Joyce Meyer
The Spiritual Emerson: Essential Works by Ralph Waldo Emerson (regarding spiritual experience)
The Serpent and the Dove: Reclaiming the Creative Spirit in the Age of Science by Dale Sides
